_comment: ANTIPATTERN 1 - entry criterion on the rule's own output field. This is the single most common cause of the cyclic-dependency error, and it is redundant: FinDock already skips a rule whose output field is non-blank.
name: Find installment by reference (self-dependency)

_comment: ANTIPATTERN 2 + 3 - a two-rule cycle (this reads Payment_Profile__c, the next writes it and reads Contact__c), and a managedRuleSet reference that would make the whole block read-only.
name: Contact from payment profile

_comment: ANTIPATTERN 4 - managed rule set reference: every rule it expands to becomes read-only, non-reorderable and non-deletable in the Guided Matching Setup UI.
ANTIPATTERN 5 - forwardToSource is injected at runtime and stripped on save; never store it. ANTIPATTERN 6 - manually flagging a rule managed.
name: Manage Source

_comment: ANTIPATTERN 7 - missing id (the order map is keyed by id; a null id blanks the seqNr and the save throws the cyclic-dependency error). ANTIPATTERN 8 - wrong id on processInstallment.
name: Set target
